paper.title: How the Brain Feels the Hurt of Heartbreak: Examining the Neurobiological Overlap Between Social and Physical Pain

claims.text: Social pain (the distress experienced when social ties are threatened or lost) is elaborated by the same neural and neurochemical substrates involved in processing physical pain.
claims.evidence: social pain – the profound distress experienced when social ties are absent, threatened, damaged, or lost – is elaborated by the same neural and neurochemical substrates involved in processing physical pain

claims.text: The evolutionarily ancient pain signal may have been co-opted to alert humans and other social mammals to the possibility of damage to social relationships, just as physical pain alerts to bodily injury.
claims.evidence: the evolutionarily ancient pain signal, which serves to limit damage to the body, may have been co-opted to alert humans and other social mammals to the possibility of damage to one's social relationships

claims.text: Morphine attenuates social separation distress (as indexed by distress vocalizations) in a variety of animal species at low, nonsedative doses.
claims.evidence: Morphine...attenuates social separation distress (as indexed by a characteristic call termed a distress vocalization) in a variety of animal species...with low, nonsedative doses of morphine

claims.text: Opioid receptor antagonists, which aggravate physical pain, increase distress vocalizations in isolated animals and slow the reduction in distress vocalizations when animals are reunited with companions.
claims.evidence: opioid receptor antagonists, which are known to aggravate physical pain...increase distress vocalizations in isolated animals...and slow the reduction in distress vocalizations typically seen when animals are reunited

claims.text: Elimination of the μ-opioid receptor through genetic engineering causes deficits in attachment, including lack of distress vocalizing.
claims.evidence: elimination of the m-opioid receptor through genetic engineering causes deficits in attachment, including lack of distress vocalizing

claims.text: Lesions of the dorsal and ventral sections of the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) reduce distress vocalization rates in animals, while electrical stimulation of the ACC triggers distress vocalizations.
claims.evidence: lesions of the dorsal and ventral sections of the ACC reduce distress vocalization rates...whereas electrical stimulation of the ACC triggers distress vocalizations

claims.text: During social exclusion in the Cyberball paradigm, participants showed increased activation in the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC) and anterior insula (AI), with dACC activation positively correlating with self-reported feelings of rejection.
claims.evidence: participants who stopped receiving ball tosses...showed increased activation in the dACC and AI...participants' feelings of rejection positively correlated with dACC activation

claims.text: The affective component of physical pain (processed in the dACC and anterior insula) is more directly involved in social pain experience than the sensory component, although the sensory component plays a role in certain types of social pain.
claims.evidence: it is probable that the affective component of physical pain is more directly involved in social pain experience, although the sensory component has been shown to play a role in certain types of social pain

claims.text: Social separation causes a painful, low-opioid state that motivates social proximity seeking and is terminated once social contact is resumed, which prompts the release of endogenous opioids.
claims.evidence: social separation causes a painful, low-opioid state that motivates social proximity seeking and is terminated once social contact is resumed, which prompts the release of endogenous opioids

claims.text: Cingulate ablation in mice causes deficits in maternal behavior, and lesions to the ACC in monkeys lead to decreases in social interest and proximity seeking.
claims.evidence: cingulate ablation in mice causes deficits in maternal behavior...and lesions to the ACC (both dorsal and ventral regions) in monkeys leads to decreases in social interest and proximity seeking
